headline.title: Ford rehires ‘gray beard’ engineers after AI falls short
headline.summary: Ford has re-hired experienced engineers, referred to as "gray beards," after finding that their initial reliance on artificial intelligence did not meet quality expectations. The company acknowledged that simply implementing AI was insufficient for achieving desired product standards.

articles.title: Prosecutors used ChatGPT logs as evidence in the Palisades fire trial
articles.summary: Prosecutors in the Palisades fire trial utilized ChatGPT logs as part of their evidence against Jonathan Rinderknecht, who is charged with arson for a deadly wildfire in Los Angeles on New Year's Day 2025. In addition to ChatGPT data, the prosecution presented location data from Rinderknecht's iPhone, security camera footage, and witness testimony to support their case.

articles.title: Why Wall Street thinks US memory maker Micron is the next Nvidia
articles.summary: Wall Street investors are increasingly optimistic about Micron Technology, viewing it as a potential successor to Nvidia in the AI sector. The company's focus on memory solutions positions it favorably as demand for AI-related technologies continues to grow.

articles.title: SoftBank’s CEO isn’t the only one with questions about Elon Musk’s orbital data center hype
articles.summary: SoftBank's CEO and other industry leaders express skepticism regarding Elon Musk's plans for orbital data centers, questioning the feasibility and practicality of the concept. Critics highlight concerns about the technological and economic viability of such projects in the current landscape.

articles.title: Margaret Atwood says the problem with AI is ‘garbage in, garbage out’
articles.summary: Margaret Atwood discussed the limitations of AI during an interview at the Babell Literary and Cultural Festival in Porto, Portugal, emphasizing the concept of "garbage in, garbage out." She highlighted her own experiences with AI, underscoring concerns about the quality of input data affecting the output.

articles.title: Why is Apple asking me to pay more for Big Tech’s AI obsession?
articles.summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook attributed recent price increases on products like the 16-inch MacBook Pro and 11-inch iPad Air to the rising costs associated with Big Tech's focus on artificial intelligence. The company has raised prices across various products, with the MacBook Pro increasing by $300 and the iPad Air by $150.

articles.title: The fittest founder in the room got cancer. Here’s how he used AI to fight back.
articles.summary: Connor Christou, a founder diagnosed with cancer, utilized AI by inputting his medical data and personal health metrics into Claude to assist in managing his treatment. This approach allowed him to analyze and optimize his health regimen during his battle with the disease.

articles.title: Asian AI startups launch Mythos-like models as Anthropic’s export ban drags on
articles.summary: Asian AI startups are introducing new models with capabilities similar to Mythos, circumventing concerns related to export bans affecting U.S. companies. This development may significantly impact the market share of American AI labs in the region.

articles.title: Apple Vision Pro exec is reportedly leaving for OpenAI
articles.summary: Paul Meade, the Apple vice president overseeing the Vision Pro headset, is reportedly departing the company to join OpenAI's hardware team. His transition highlights ongoing talent movement within the tech industry as companies expand their AI capabilities.
